walkthrough:
In the right-angled cross-section of the cone, apply Pythagoras' theorem with slant height $15\text{ cm}$ and vertical height $h\text{ cm}$:
$$r^2 + h^2 = 15^2 \implies r^2 = 225 - h^2$$

Substitute $r^2$ into the cone volume formula:
$$V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^2 h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(225 - h^2)h = \frac{1}{3}\pi(225h - h^3)$$

Differentiate the volume function with respect to $h$:
$$\frac{dV}{dh} = \frac{1}{3}\pi(225 - 3h^2) = \pi(75 - h^2)$$

Set $\frac{dV}{dh} = 0$ to locate stationary values:
$$\pi(75 - h^2) = 0 \implies h^2 = 75 \implies h = \sqrt{75} = 5\sqrt{3} \approx 8.66\text{ cm} \quad (\text{since } h > 0)$$

Determine the nature using the second derivative:
$$\frac{d^2V}{dh^2} = \frac{1}{3}\pi(-6h) = -2\pi h$$
$$\text{At } h = 5\sqrt{3}: \quad \frac{d^2V}{dh^2} = -10\sqrt{3}\pi < 0$$
Since $\frac{d^2V}{dh^2} < 0$, the volume is a **local maximum**.
